Atrocity

uh-TROS-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Atrocity is an extremely wicked, cruel, or brutal act.

The novel's most gripping chapter forces the narrator to finally speak the name of the atrocity he witnessed as a boy.

Worked Example

The museum's exhibit forces visitors to confront the full scale of the atrocity, from the burned villages to the thousands of names on the memorial wall.

Atrocity describes acts so cruel and brutal that they shock the conscience -- far beyond ordinary wrongdoing.

How Atrocity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

barbarity

barbarity: extreme cruelty or brutality

outrage

outrage: an action that is shockingly wrong or immoral

Antonyms

kindness

kindness: the quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate

benevolence

benevolence: a desire to do good to others

How Strong Is It? — wrongdoing → genocide → atrocity

wrongdoing vs. atrocity

wrongdoing vs. atrocity: Wrongdoing is a general term for any bad or illegal act, far milder and broader than the shocking cruelty of an atrocity.

genocide vs. atrocity

genocide vs. atrocity: Genocide is an even more extreme atrocity, the deliberate mass killing of an entire group of people.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — atroc-

root — atroc-: cruel, fierce, terrible (Latin atrox)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Atrocity comes from Latin atrox ('cruel, fierce'), the same root behind the everyday adjective atrocious, plus -ity -- 'the state or quality of being cruel,' or an act showing that cruelty.

Use the root in a new word: atrocious

Use the root in a new word: atrocious: Critics called the film's special effects atrocious, calling them the worst they'd seen all year.

Root Check

Word Choice

Atrocity is a strong, serious word almost always reserved for real cruelty or violence -- it should never be used casually to describe a minor annoyance.
